verses.1: The word of the LORD that came to Zephaniah son of Cushi, son of Gedaliah, son of Amariah, son of Hezekiah, in the days of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah.
verses.2: I will sweep away all from the face of the earth, says the LORD.
verses.3: I will sweep away people and beasts, birds of the sky and fish of the sea, together with the wicked and the sinners, and I will cut off humanity from the face of the earth, says the LORD.
verses.4: I will stretch out my hand against Judah and against all who dwell in Jerusalem. I will cut off from this place the names of Baal, the names of the priests,
verses.5: and those who bow on the rooftops to the army of heaven, and those who swear by the LORD and swear by the king,
verses.6: and those who turn away from the LORD, those who do not seek the LORD, nor look for him.
verses.7: Be silent before the Lord GOD, for the day of the LORD is near. The LORD has prepared his sacrifice, he has consecrated his invited ones.
verses.8: And on the day of the LORD’s sacrifice I will punish the rulers, and the king’s sons, and all who wear foreign garments.
verses.9: I will punish all who leap over the threshold on that day, those who fill their master’s house with violence and deceit.
verses.10: And on that day, says the LORD, a cry will come from the Fish Gate, a wail from the Second Quarter, and a great breaking from the hills.
verses.11: Wail, you who live in the fortress! For all the people of Canaan are silenced; all those who weigh silver are cut off.
verses.12: And on that day I will search Jerusalem with lamps and punish those who sit complacently in their complacency, those who say in their hearts, “The LORD will not do good, nor will he do harm.”
verses.13: Their might will be for plunder, their homes for desolation. They will build houses but not live in them; they will plant vineyards but not drink their wine.
verses.14: The great day of the LORD is near, it is near and coming swiftly. The voice of the day of the LORD is bitter, a warrior cries there.
verses.15: That day will be a day of wrath, a day of trouble and distress, a day of ruin and devastation, a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and thick darkness.
verses.16: A day of the trumpet and war-cry against the fortified cities and the high towers.
verses.17: And I will distress humanity, and they will walk like the blind, because they have sinned against the LORD. Their blood will be poured out like dust, and their flesh like dung.
verses.18: Neither their silver nor their gold will be able to save them on the day of the LORD’s wrath. In the fire of his jealousy, the entire earth will be consumed, for the LORD will accomplish his work swiftly and with alarm for all who live on the earth.

notes:
Notes  
- v. 1: The Hebrew lineage is rendered clearly, preserving the full chain of names in English.  
- v. 4: "Names of the priests" may refer to the titles or roles associated with the Baal worship, not the priests themselves.  
- v. 6: "Those who do not seek the LORD, nor look for him" reflects the parallel structure in the Hebrew, using distinct verbs for clarity.  
- v. 10: "Fish Gate" is a translation of שַׁעַר הַדָּגִים, a known gate in Jerusalem. "Second Quarter" (מִשְׁנֶה) may refer to a district or area in the city.  
- v. 11: "Canaan" is used as a metaphor for a people or group, not necessarily the ancient nation.  
- v. 17: "Walk like the blind" is a rendering of the Hebrew idiom for people deprived of understanding or guidance.
